summary: Rotate a linked list to the right by k places.
mainInsight: Rotating right by k moves the last k nodes to the front. Find the length n, reduce k modulo n, make the list circular, then cut it at the node n - k - 1 steps from the head.
canonicalApproach: Close into a ring and cut

approaches.name: Rotate one step k times
approaches.summary: Move the tail to the front repeatedly.

approaches.name: Close into a ring and cut
approaches.summary: Connect tail to head; walk n - k - 1 steps; cut.

approaches.name: Two pointers k apart
approaches.summary: Advance fast k nodes, then move both until fast is the tail.

personalSolution.approach: Close into a ring and cut

promptVariants: What technique turns a rotation into one cut?
How do you avoid rotating k times when k is huge?
options: Reduce k modulo the length and cut a circular list
Reverse the list twice, once per half of the cut
Sort the nodes by position and relink them
Use recursion k times, rotating by a single node each time
cards.answer: Reduce k modulo the length and cut a circular list
cards.explanation: A rotation by n is the identity, so only k % n matters.

promptVariants: Why is the new tail at n - k - 1 steps from the head?
cards.answer: After rotating right by k, the old (n - k)-th node becomes the tail and the next node becomes the new head. Starting at the head (index 0), the node at index n - k - 1 is that new tail; set its next to None and return the node after it.
cards.explanation: The circular link keeps the old tail connected to the old head.
One pass to find the length and one partial pass to the cut point.

promptVariants: Why return early when `k %= n` becomes 0, and why must the ring be broken again?
What would happen if you forgot `new_tail.next = None`?
cards.code:
k %= n
if k == 0:
    return head
tail.next = head
new_tail = head
for _ in range(n - k - 1):
    new_tail = new_tail.next
new_head = new_tail.next
new_tail.next = None
cards.answer: k % n == 0 means a full rotation, so the list is unchanged and we avoid building the ring. After linking tail -> head the structure is a cycle; cutting new_tail.next = None restores a proper null-terminated list. Without it traversal would loop forever.
keyPoints: Forgetting the cut creates a cycle
cards.explanation: Edge cases: empty list, single node, k = 0 are handled up front.

promptVariants: For [10,20,30,40] and k = 6 what is the result?
Why does k larger than n still work?
cards.explanation: 6 % 4 = 2: the last two nodes move to the front.

incorrectOptionExplanations.[10,20,30,40]: That would be k = 0 (or a multiple of the length).
incorrectOptionExplanations.[40,10,20,30]: That rotates by only one place.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[20,30,40,10]: That rotates left by one instead of right by two.
